contest.choosing_rule: Rules whose P10-P90 ranges caught the actual total in 75% to 85% of back-test cases are eligible. Among them the lowest median absolute error is the best; the simplest eligible rule within 5% of that error wins. If no rule is eligible, the rule whose coverage is closest to 80% wins. This rule was fixed in assumptions/backtest.yaml before any score was computed.

origins.note: The 21 rolling origins overlap: each shares up to 4 of its 5 target years with the next. They hold about 5 non-overlapping 5-year periods, so case counts overstate the independent evidence; read coverage and error as resting on about 5 periods, not 21.

sentences: Philadelphia: 2021 permits (25,257 units) were 7.7 times the median of its other years in 2021-2025 (3,294), so a mean of that window is pulled up by one year; a median is not.

stress.sentence: If the next five years look like the 12 past boom periods (origins 1999, 2000, 2001, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019), the baseline's likely range is 115,122 units to 169,715 units (middle 151,882 units).

findings: 7 rules were back-tested on the same 1,395 county cases. The top-down share won: it was typically 41% off, its ranges caught the real total in 54% of cases, and it ran 28% high on average. No rule's coverage was inside the band, so the closest to 80% won.
The five-year mean was typically 39% off and ran 23% high.
The three-year mean had the lowest error but did not win: its coverage (52%) was outside the band.

Out of time (each origin corrected only with errors known by then; 993 cases), the winner's own projection was typically 48% off. Correcting it by size class gave 63% with ranges that caught 55%; by place type, 65% and 51%. The engine uses size-class pools: place-type pools did not lower the out-of-time error.
Ranges built from past errors caught the real total less often when tested on later years than when tested on other counties: a new housing cycle moves every county at once.

The winner was chosen on the whole back-test (every origin at once), so the choice itself is in-sample; its ranges and the corrections are scored only with errors from earlier origins. Size classes are worked out at each origin from the years up to it; place types are today's county grouping (current data) applied to every origin.
In small counties the five-year mean ran 43% high and the top-down share runs 49% high; its ranges caught 198 of 344 cases.
In medium counties the five-year mean ran 25% high and the top-down share runs 30% high; its ranges caught 184 of 330 cases.
In 'Big-city, growing, higher-cost' counties the five-year mean ran 53% low and the top-down share runs 61% low; its ranges caught 3 of 15 cases. Few cases: read this as a few places, not a pattern.
In 'Rural, steady, lower-cost' counties the five-year mean ran 34% high and the top-down share runs 39% high; its ranges caught 235 of 405 cases.

In 'Rural, slow-growth, lower-cost' counties the five-year mean ran 170% high and the top-down share runs 416% high; its ranges caught 5 of 29 cases. Few cases: read this as a few places, not a pattern.
In rural counties the five-year mean ran 33% high and the top-down share runs 40% high; its ranges caught 279 of 524 cases.
In counties with a lower share of Qualified Census Tracts the five-year mean ran 29% high and the top-down share runs 35% high; its ranges caught 285 of 510 cases.
In Philadelphia the five-year mean ran 53% low and the top-down share runs 61% low; its ranges caught 3 of 15 cases. Few cases: read this as a few places, not a pattern.
Philadelphia: 2021 permits (25,257 units) were 7.7 times the median of its other years in 2021-2025 (3,294), so a mean of that window is pulled up by one year; a median is not.
In the back-test, the rule ran 65% low for Philadelphia in the 5 cases whose target years hold a surge year, and 57% low in the other 16.
